Definition: Tsalmonah, a place in the Desert
BiblicalUsage: Tsalmonah was a camp of Israel in the wilderness, between Mount Hor and Punon on the long journey to the promised land. The stations are listed in order, and Tsalmonah is one of the quiet stops between the better-known ones. It is named twice, in the same two verses, as the place where they set out and where they came.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the wilderness stations matter because God counted every camp — none of the journey was wasted, and none of it was forgotten. Tsalmonah is proof that the quiet stops are part of the road.
